utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, good morning to you. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning to you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours and also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with Ms. Joanne Richardson and our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink. And I apologise, but later on this morning, Ms. Patricia Sellers will join the team as well. She will be a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends. My name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. I understand there has been a problem raised by the Defence. I'm copied into it. The Defence wrote to the Prosecution that they have been unable to locate the following exhibits on the electronic data system, and nor has the Prosecution disclosed the following documents. We have a list of them here. I will go through them for the sake of the record, ERN numbers 0345-5109, 0109-7642, 0345-5118, 0345-5107, 0345-5114. It also says that -- the rest is not important to read. So what's the position on this? I take it now -- yes, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Well, we don't in fact have -- still don't have copies of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is serious.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, it's -- and I'm getting fed up, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well indeed, Your Honour. The position is we did search the EDS system, two of our legal assistants searched and we were not able to find these documents. And we left messages, voice messages, for the Prosecution to help us with this matter. The Prosecution this morning in our discussions with them are maintaining that those documents are on EDS but we have been looking for them and we simply cannot find them. In those circumstances I propose firstly that on the next occasion we would suggest that a member of the Registry or the Chambers sit with us and we'll demonstrate that these documents are not there. That we are not able to find them. Because otherwise I don't see how we are going to resolve a situation where the Prosecution simply assert that it's on the EDS and we are unable to find it. But in any event, since this is an issue, it would also seem to be a matter of pure courtesy that actually copies would be provided for us and left in our locker and I would suggest certainly for the future that that should be done on each occasion that the Prosecution intend to use exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And that's why it was further greatly annoying that we weren't able to reach anyone last night. We all have mobile phones and the first call which my legal assistant made was at 6.30 and I don't think it's open for the Prosecution to send off the exhibit list and then to be unreachable because obviously if we have questions we need to be able to reach them on their mobile phones and maybe resolve the platter without having to bring it for the attention of the Trial Chamber. So I think it would only be reasonable to expect the Prosecution firstly to be available in the evenings after they have sent out their exhibit lists for these sorts of queries and secondly to leave courtesy copies of the documents they intend to use because EDS is not a complete answer to these issues. As we have seen there are problems with EDS and EDS, in a sense, is also an optional adjunct to the whole disclosure system. And we have a right to be provided with copies of the documents the Prosecution intends to use. That's the position. We don't have the documents still and I wouldn't intend to close my examination in chief until I've seen those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The thing is that I notice, having gone through the Prosecution list, unless there is an updated list that I am not aware of, and your letter or communication to the Prosecution that as regards 03455107 and 03455114, I don't really see them in the Prosecution list of exhibits. Maybe I am missing something but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well that's the other matter I was going to raise, Your Honour, which is that there are documents which they haven't been tendered as exhibits. We don't know the source, we don't know if they have been typed up the day before by Serb intelligence and we see documents in Cyrillic with stamps which seem rather doubtful to us. So we -- my second point I was going to make this morning is we certainly intend to object strongly to the authenticity of several of these documents, particularly where they have never been tendered by the Prosecution investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The other matter is I understand that the Prosecution may be alleging that some of these documents have been disclosed previously and that's certainly something which at this stage anyway we deny. We will check that allegation. But certainly we are not aware of any of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That can be verified. I mean, that can be easily verified easily. So I thank you, Mr. Jones, for bringing this to the attention of the Trial Chamber. Who is responding? Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first part regarding communications, and that's the communications between lead counsel, I respond to it and then I will give the floor to Ms. Joanne Richardson for the further details. I learned of this issue this morning, only this morning. Yesterday I was available in the office until around 8.00 in the evening, and I have not been contacting regarding this issue until this very morning. And then I learned, as I also was aware, that Ms. Joanne Richardson was available at her office with -- at least my telephone number is available to lead counsel and also Mr. Jones knows my telephone number and how to touch base with me. So this comes for a surprise that they were not able to contact me and as it was always been a good communication when there are problems and solved between lead counsel or counsel, I was fully aware when I learned of this, this morning, that I was available but had not been contacted. For further details I will now ask Ms. Joanne Richardson to make her submission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson? Thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours and good morning to the Defence. Your Honour, it's -- I just learned of the situation this morning myself. I was in my office until extremely late last night and I did not get a call from the Defence. It is my understanding that they did try to contact our case manager who herself has advised me that her -- both her home number and cell and office number has been available to the Defence. I don't know what the miscommunication is with regards to them trying to contact us but I know I was in my office until almost 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go to the crux of the matter, these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And secondly, Your Honour, it's my understanding that the documents are on the EDS and they were disclosed in a regular disclosure disk to the Defence. It's also my understanding that there was a discussion this morning between our case manager and the legal assistant of the Defence team and we advised that documents were placed in the locker last evening, not all of them, at least two, and we were making copies of the others and this is in response to their assertions that they do not have them and cannot locate them on EDS, although it's my understanding that they are. What I can do Your Honour is simply put off using those documents in my cross-examination later on today until the Defence has had an opportunity to review them, and I can use them tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That may be one solution. On the other hand, it's beyond me, and I'm being extremely frank and blunt at the same time with you. It's beyond me how you can even disagree on whether these documents are on the EDS -- available on the EDS system or not. One side is saying definite they are not. And please let's sit down together and check. The other one is saying, yes, they are definitely in. The Trial Chamber should never be put in this position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Never, never. That's number 1. And secondly, if you are so sure that they have been disclosed on a CD to the Defence, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are looking into that -- as, again, this was only raised this morning. We only learned of it. So we will look into the receipt of the disclosures that we've provided to them on the CD. And also, double check to see if it is in EDS and confirm our statements to you this morning. Outside of that, I can't provide you with any other explanation at this point other than we feel that we fulfil our obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't extract explanations if you don't have them, obviously. I mean, so, but let's work it out this way. You will not make use of these documents today when you start the cross-examination. And we will, of course, reserve the rights of the Prosecution -- of the Defence to put further questions which may arise out of these documents. In the meantime, while it is being understood that you will not make use of these documents preferably not make use of these documents today, from experience, the situation might change if you find these documents in the first place. You should have them available if you had in mind to use them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have them. Copies are being made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Make copies of them and hand them over to the Defence and also to us to put us in a position to make an assessment and maybe, after seeing the contents of these documents, the Defence might not even object to your making use of them today and we can -- I'm going to use a heavy word, plod forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's exactly what we advised the Defence this morning, that copies would be made and they would be given to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, but -- yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, firstly just if in future any documents which the Prosecution intend to use which are not exhibits, if they could simply place that in our locker then already that will go a long way to solve this problem. Secondly, I must admit I'm baffled if the Prosecution is saying that the CaseMap manager didn't receive messages on her phone. We left messages, and if that's being denied then we really do any need to look into -- into this, because I was present while my assistant left messages. So I'm not sure the Prosecution is denying receiving messages from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam. I didn't understand it that way. What I understood Ms. Richardson to say is that there's no denial that messages were left for Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink, but that she has in any case forwarded you, made available to you, all her telephone numbers, including home, apparently, and mobile telephone. That's how I understood it. I didn't understand that there was a statement denying what you had stated, that you had left a message.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Richardson said that her case -- CaseMap manager had "herself advised me that both her home number and cell and office number had been available to the Defence. I don't know what the communication is with regards to them trying to contact us." Well, available, we left messages on those numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I certainly would not --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not at all -- and I -- clearly, as Mr. Jones has just repeated my -- what I said. I've never said that they didn't leave messages. What I said, there's some kind of miscommunication and that Ms. Henry-Frijlink's telephone numbers are available. She said she did not receive a message at home, but we were both here very late yesterday and they could have left it on her cell number which she didn't receive immediately so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's close it -- let's close it here, Mr. Jones, for the time being and continue with the evidence. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We did leave a message on her cell number as well. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Jones. I mean, I do not doubt it for a moment. But sometimes -- and it happens to me sometimes -- I do get SMS messages, for example, three days afterwards. And phone messages a day or two later. I mean, it has happened to me. So here in the Netherlands, because it doesn't happen anywhere else, to be honest with you, but it does happen here. Sometimes I get voice messages two days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The other preliminary concerns the interview of our client which I wanted to just mention briefly as well before the witness comes in. Right from the start of this trial, we've been asking for there to be a corrected translation of the interview. In reviewing the interview again, we've noticed wide discrepancies between the Bosnian and the English on extremely important matters, in some cases where exculpatory material has literally been edited out or in any event is not present in the English even though it's in the Bosnian. And in an a segment which apparently the Prosecution intends to use, there is very serious discrepancy which I certainly would intend to raise. But I can wait until that arises in cross-examination. But we'll ask for the witness at that stage to leave and deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's a very serious matter and we intend to raise it, possibly eventually in a motion because there are large numbers of inaccuracies and discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps Mr. Jones --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jones, for raising this matter and being ethically very correct about it too. Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just would like at the time that we address this for Mr. Jones, to provide exactly which interview he's referring to because there are a number of statements given by this witness. So just to clarify for us to be sure we are all talking about the same interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can do that after the -- during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I'll do it when it arises, when I see which section they intend to use. There are so many discrepancies I can't possibly identify them all right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime try to procure these copies as -- a.s.a.p, please, all right?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, they are being done this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Madam Registrar, could you please bring the witness in, escort the witness? And we have lost 20 minutes, 22 minutes. While the witness is still on his way, you probably are already aware because you should be notified -- I don't know -- but there is a submission of the Registry in several cases, including this case, pursuant to Rule 33(B) of the rules of procedure, regarding Defence motion seeking access to confidential material in several cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you received it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I believe so. We'll check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But it contains some very interesting material, and if you wish to provide us with an input from your part on the matter, we'll certainly take it into consideration. The same applies to the Prosecution, of course, needless to say. All right? This is a document that was filed on the 28th of October, in the following, in the Hadzihasanovic, the Slobodan Milosevic, the Blagojevic, this case, Prlic, which hasn't started, Delic which Madam Vidovic knows about, and Miletic, all right? This is where it has been filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. Sacirovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We are going to continue with your testimony this morning. And I'm actually immediately calling upon Mr. Jones to proceed with his questions. May I just reminds you that you are testifying under oath pursuant to the solemn declaration that you entered yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And good morning from me, Mr. Sacirovic.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yesterday you gave evidence about certain films, certain things which you filmed, and information which you gathered. And we saw some of those videos. Did you film a session of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I'm moving to a different subject now. Did you know someone in Srebrenica called Kemo?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several men called Kemo.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know a Kemo from Pale?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know Kemo from Pale, from the time I spent in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know what his full name was?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kemal Mehmedovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When you saw him, was he in any sort of uniform?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When you saw him, was he armed?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was he a fighter in an organised unit, so far as you know, this is in the period 1992, up to demilitarisation.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was at Pale, until July 1992, he was a civilian. He worked with a tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown D573. I'm moving to a new area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, this is just to read into the record, it's Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Srebrenica municipality, War Presidency, Srebrenica, 3 April 1993. And it's a report and it starts off, "We wish to take this opportunity to inform in detail all those to whom we are writing of events on the Srebrenica front between 20 January and 3 April 1993." Now, firstly, were you in Srebrenica in that period, from 20 January 1993, to the 3rd of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were you still gathering information for your commission during that period?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And where were you gathering information?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica. In this period, I spent most of the time in the hospital there because the wounded were brought in every day and that's where I got the latest and most accurate information.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: From speaking to the wounded?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, for the benefit of everyone we are going to review the situation in this period, entry by entry, with reference to documents from the Serbian Drina Corps. So I'm going to start by reading the entries and directing your attention, Mr. Sacirovic, to the entries for 21st to 24th January 1993 and the 25th of January 1993, and I'll just read that. 21 to 24 January 1993, shelling of the free territory of Srebrenica. 25 January 1993, "the aggressor launched a large offensive against the free territory of Srebrenica, engaging strong forces of the Uzice Corps -- sorry, Uzice and Valjevo Corps, mechanised armoured and infantry forces that crossed the bridge in Skelani and the Parucac dam. The aggressor occupied and then completely torched the villages of Poljak, Milicevici, Jagodnja, and Joseva, massacring 80 civilians and wounding over 40." Do you see those entries?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do they accurately state the situation at the time, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, if you keep that document with you for a moment, we have a new exhibit, the ERN is 04273560. And it's, I believe, not a complete translation but just of the relevant parts. This is the translation as we received it. This is from the Drina Corps Command, dated 23 January 1993, to the commands of all corps units. And it's a combat order signed by commander Colonel Milenko Zivanovic, and I need to read paragraphs 3 and 4 into the record. Paragraph 3, "The VRS GS reserve will launch an offensive in central Podrinje, grouping their main forces on the Bratunac-Potocari village - Srebrenica - the bauxite mine, Gunjaci village axis,, and the auxiliary ones on the Skelani village, Osmace village, Zeleni Jadar village, Srebrenica axis to perform the following task: In a coordinated action it our corps forces smash and destroy the enemy forces in the general area of Srebrenica, liberate the Sase and Gunjaci mines and cut the green transversal in the general area of Srebrenica. Then in a coordinated action with our corps forces, gradually destroy the enemy in the general areas of Cerska and Zepa. And then paragraph 4, "I've decided: Launch an attack with the main forces on the Milici, Suceska, Podravanje village, Zvornik, Kamenica, Cerska, Olovo Kamenica village, Rudo, Medjedja village, Visegrad, Medjedja village, and Rogatica Medjedja village axes, and with the auxiliary forces at the lines reached, engage in persistent Defence and active combat operations on these axes and tie up as many enemy forces as possible, inflicting as many losses as possible with the aim of creating the best possible conditions for a speedy breakthrough of the VRS GS reserve, and smashing and destroying the enemy forces in the Srebrenica, Cerska, and Zepa sectors." Now, I have several questions arising from this. First, do you agree that this is a combat order for a coordinated offencive across the whole of the enclave, Kamenica, Cerska, Konjevic Polje, Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If we go to paragraph 5, unit tasks, "The Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade with reinforcement units, after the necessary regrouping of forces, will launch an attack with the main forces on the Drmno village, Glogova village, Kravica axis. Its task - in a coordinated action with part of the VRS GS reserve - is to take control of the Velika Glogova village, Halilovici village sector, and then continue the attack and take control of the Kravica village sector. Once Kravica village, the Sase mine, and Srebrenica are controlled, mop the area of any enemy forces left behind and isolated, and create conditions to establish authority. "Support provided by the artillery of the VRS GS reserve." Now, I want you to just concentrate on the words there, "once Kravica village, the Sase mine and Srebrenica are controlled, mop the area of any enemy forces left behind and isolate it." My question to this. The stated aim of this combat order is, in fact, to take Srebrenica entirely, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And what do the words "mop the area of any enemy forces left behind" mean to you in this context?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means to eliminate all manpower because all the other features that existed there had been long destroyed. This means that any manpower found or living beings found should be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In other words, what happened in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And we see at the end of that paragraph the words "support provided by the artillery of the VRS GS reserve." What can you tell us about the use of artillery by the Serbs against the Srebrenica pocket in late January 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The free territory of Srebrenica was shelled from all available assets in the hands of the army of Republika Srpska, or rather the former Yugoslav People's Army, from all directions. To put it simply, it was shelled from Serbia and from all the Serb-held territories surrounding the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll ask for an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the next number is D8 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D878, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 878. So this document, which in the B/C/S version consists of five pages starting with ERN 04273560 up to and inclusive of 04273564, and 3 pages in English is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D878. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And we have a new exhibit to distribute which is ERN 04273566. And while that's being passed around, Mr. Sacirovic, in your evidence yesterday, you stated that you heard about units arriving from Novi Sad and Valjevo. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Where is Valjevo?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Valjevo is located in Serbia. To be more precise, some 70 or 80 kilometres away from the Drina River, Bratunac and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And we saw reference, do we not, to the Valjevo Corps in the entry of for 25 January 1993 in the document we saw earlier, D573?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to read this document into the record. It's from the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade command dated 24 January 1993. It's addressed to the Drina Corps command, the VRS Main Staff, the commander personally, "In accordance with a verbal order and with regard to a report submitted on the means of support for the units of the Zvornik and Bratunac Brigades," and then a list follows. "One, ammunition: Shells/rockets, one combat set each for all requested equipment," and then there is a list of various calibres of artillery. "2. Four 82-millimetre recoilless gun, one combat set each for the Bratunac Brigade. "3. Four 122-millimetre M-38 howitzers for the Zvornik Brigade. "4. Taking of ten T-34 tanks for the Zvornik Brigade (two taken because of crews). And then "5. The following units have arrived in the area between Loznicka and Ljubovija, an armoured mechanised battalion in Loznicka, 122-millimetre battery in Radalj, a tank and mechanised company in the Ljubovija area, 122-millimetre M-38 howitzer battery, 128-millimetre Oganj VBR battery in Ljubovija, a military police company in the Mali Zvornik area, a reconnaissance company in the Mali Zvornik-Ljubovija area, 120-millimetre rocket launcher battery in the Ljubovija area, two 128-millimetre self-propelled rocket launcher in the Ljubovija area, an engineer's company in the Mali Zvornik Ljubovija area and then the command post of the brigade from Valjevo, the KM of the Drina, OG, from Valjevo, first army IKM, forward command post in the Ljubovija area." And it's signed by Colonel Milutin Skocajic. Now, does this document firstly confirm that on the 24th of January 1993, units among others from Valjevo had arrived to provide support for the units of the Zvornik and Bratunac Brigades?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you yourself hear about the arrival of these units and these vast amounts of artillery in the area in late January 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I've already indicated yesterday, we were listening in through the makeshift radio to the Bratunac radio where we obtained very important information. Very often, they stated that reinforcements from Serbia were on the way, probably even to raise their morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There is a list here of a number of artillery batteries which is in the transcript so I don't need to repeat it. But looking, for example, at the 122-millimetre M-38 howitzer battery and the 128-millimetre VBR multiple-rocket launcher battery, can you assist the Trial Chamber with how much damage the amounts of artillery mentioned here can do to property, from your experience?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This type of ammunition destroys human beings, immovable features; to put it simply, it can destroy a whole town.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In what sort of a period can it destroy a whole town? How long can that take with this amount of artillery?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what is stated here, it would take less than an hour to raze an entire town if all the assets mentioned here are engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know if Your Honour is willing to accept that artillery pieces and mortars can cause fire. It's something which I've been wondering whether I need to pursue with witnesses or whether it's such an obvious point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To be honest with you, I am not interfering in any way in the questions you ask to this and to other witnesses but certain areas definitely have been abundantly covered. This is one of them definitely. We have heard from other witnesses the effects of Zoljas, of --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you don't -- you don't need to -- I mean, you're free to ask any questions you like but I don't think you need to labour much on these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unless it is of course contested strenuously by the Prosecution which I don't think it is. Yes, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Certainly, I don't believe the Prosecution has accepted the Defence position that all of the damage done to the various --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not what I'm saying. What --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I misunderstood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's whether you accept or not that, if you fire a Zolja into a building, or if artillery and certain -- particularly certain kinds of artillery is directed at houses, that would cause a fire. This is the -- it's a purely technical issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe at this point the Defence -- excuse me, the Prosecution, will accept the entirety of the Defence's proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's a very practical approach, Ms. Richardson. Mr. Jones, please go as deep as you like into this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you've heard what the Trial Chamber thinks.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll just ask this, Mr. Sacirovic: Can artillery pieces and mortars start fires in houses?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Most of the artillery pieces are contained -- contain charges of different purposes. They have shaped charges that can penetrate and pierce steel. They have rockets that can be ignited from artillery pieces. I am not a military expert. However, from my experience in Srebrenica, I arrived at the following conclusion: That they had used all sorts of projectiles, even those containing toxic charges, even those projectiles were used by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Is that something which you actually saw for yourself?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask for an exhibit number, please, for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Jones. This document, which consists of one page in B/C/S and two pages in English and with ERN 04273566 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D879. Thank you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And now we have the next document, which is ERN 04273573. And this is from the Uzice Corps Command, 25 January 1993, to the army of Republika Srpska Drina Corps Command. I'm going to take you to the -- well, the first paragraph, "We hereby inform you that by 1100 hours on 25 January 1993, the Uzice Corps forces broke out at the following axes. Radijevici village, Strazavac, to Gradina, Zabokvica village, 3, Pale village, Skejici village, and then, 2. In the Uzice Corps area of attack up to the axis of Jagodnja village, Osmaca village, Radosevici village." First, I want to pause there. Are you familiar with the place names mentioned there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Does this document confirm or not that on the 25th of January 1993, the Uzice Corps was present in actions in the Srebrenica and Skelani area in the Radijevici, Zabokvica, Pale, Jagodnja, Osmace, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was that or was that not confirmed by the information which you gathered at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd simply ask for an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document, which consists of two pages, one in B/C/S, one in English, the English being the translation of the other -- of the B/C/S one, the ERN 04273573 is being tendered and marked Defence Exhibit D880.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now I want to go back to an entry in this document, D573, the document from the War Presidency. We see the entry now for 26 January to 1 February 1993. "Shelling of the entire free territory of Srebrenica and infantry fighting on the contact lines." Now if we can look at D839, if the witness can please be shown Defence Exhibit D839 -- and this is from the Uzice Corps Command it's dated January 27, 1993, to the VRS Drina Corps Command. On the basis of the order of Yugoslav army headquarters strictly confidential number 14-1, "We would like to inform you about the following: One, Uzice Corps units will hand over the reached front lines to the Drina Corps on January 28 1993, starting at 4.00 p.m. They will withdraw on January 29-30." Now, firstly, do you agree that this document is from the Uzice Corps command signed by the commander, Major General Dragoljub Ojdanic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And can you tell us where these units of the Uzice Corps would be coming from?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came from Bajina Basta or, rather, were transported into Bosnia and Herzegovina across the Drina bridge at Bajina Basta or Skelani, and across the hydroelectric plant Perucac above Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are agreed that Bajina Basta is in Serbia. I just want to make sure that we don't need evidence about that as well. All right. Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 3, in the second subparagraph, it states, "In our combat activities so far, we inflicted huge losses to the enemy in the village of Mlecevo, Jagodnja, Joseva, the village of Daljegosta, Arapovici, the village of Pavkovici, the village of Tihici, the village of Milicevici, Osmace, the village of Tokoljak, and Jezero." Now, my question is this, are you aware whether any of those villages were in fact Serb villages before the war.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll ask you to go through the list carefully, we can deal with them one by one, if you like. Mlecevo, was that a Serb or Muslim village before the war?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mlecevo was a mixed village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Arapovici, was that Serb, Muslim or mixed before the war?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A mixed village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Pavkovici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As well, mixed village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So would it be right to understand from this document that in this period, Serb units from Serbia proper, in this case the Uzice Corps, were in fact attacking and inflicting losses on villages among which there were Serb houses before the war?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In your experience in this period, were the Serbs careful about distinguishing between Serb houses and Muslim houses when they used artillery?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And can you please enlarge on that a little and explain for Their Honours how that could be, as it might be difficult to understand.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When artillery opens fire, none of the features say or indicate in any way whether it's a Serb, Muslim or any other feature. So weapons, when they open fire, they open fire at targets. As such, none of the buildings there had any external features indicating who they belonged to except for the places of worship, mosques and churches, which, by their appearance, indicated what they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So would Serbs and Serb units from Serbia proper necessarily know which villages were Muslim and which were Serb?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we return to the War Presidency document D573 to look at the entry for 2 February 1993, which reads, "The aggressor continued the offensive against the free territory of Vlasenica, Zvornik, and Bratunac municipalities, including the Novi Sad and Drina Corps on this front. There were fierce attacks in the Voljavica region with constant shelling from Serbia and aerial fire against the free territories of there region." Now, do you see that and does that in any way reflect your experience of what was happening in that period?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd also ask you to just bear in mind what's described there while we move to the next exhibit, which is ERN 04267410. And this is from the Drina Corps Command dated 5 February 1993, it's a regular combat report to the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska army, signed by Colonel Milenko Zivanovic, commander of the Drina corps. I'm just going to read two sections and ask you to follow. First of all, paragraph 2, combat readiness, "All units are in full combat readiness. Specific tasks have been issued to the 1st and 2nd Birac Brigade and the 1st Zvornik and 1st Bratunac Brigades. They are carrying out active combat operations along several axes in order to tighten the encirclement around the enemy." If we go further down, skipping a paragraph, "The 2nd Battalion of the 1st Bratunac Brigade is carrying out active combat operations along the following axis, Zaluzje, Kunjerac, Bjelovac." And if we turn to paragraph 8, "conclusions," "Conclusions, anticipated developments, and decision for future operations. We assess that the enemy still has not abandoned the objective and desire to capture the Drina corridor. However, I believe that the enemy forces in the Cerska and Konjevic Polje and Kamenica sector are in a state of great panic and, due to this, on 4 February 1993, we issued a specific tasks to the 1st and 2nd Birac, the 1st Bratunac, and the 1st Zvornik Brigades and the Skelani Independent Battalion, specifying the axes of attack in active combat operations in order to inflict the greatest possible losses on the enemy and force them to surrender or retreat towards Kamenica." Did you follow that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is what is stated there, does that accurately reflect the situation in early February 1993 or not?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We saw in paragraph 2 a reference to "tightening the encirclement around the enemy." Is that something which you experienced or noticed in Srebrenica at the time, that in fact there was a "tightening encirclement"?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this period, every day there were wounded arriving from the ground, which indicated that the situation was chaotic, that the Serbs were attacking from all sides, against the free territory and that they were getting ever closer to Srebrenica proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask for an exhibit number, please, for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, which consists of two pages in B/C/S and three pages in English, ERN 04267410 to 411 is being tendered and received as -- and marked as Defence Exhibit D881.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And now if we go to a further entry in D573, this War Presidency document, we have an entry for the 4th to 28th of February, and it simply says, "The aggressor attacked the Cerska, Konjevic Polje, Kamenica, Glogova, Skelani, Voljavica, Suceska, and other defence lines." Again if you can confirm or not that indeed those areas mentioned there were attacked by the Serbs in February 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Serb offensive was intensifying. This can be seen from the documents, but we felt it on our own skins and the situation was becoming truly alarming.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And in that regard, we have another exhibit which is ERN 04336227. And it's Drina Corps Command dated 12 February 1993, and it's signed by the commander of the Drina corps, Colonel Milenko Jovanovic and I'm going to refer to you paragraph 4 of that document, where it reads, "I've decided to use the main forces at current positions for decisive defence to prevent an enemy breakthrough deep in the zone of responsibility of the corps from the following axes," and then places are mentioned. And then "to use the auxiliary forces, reinforcement units of the 1st KK and special operations units with strong fire support in a coordinated action with forces of the defence sector to mount an attack in the general direction of Potajnik, Hasanovici village, Macesi village, Konjevic Polje, with the aim to crush the enemy in the area of Cerska and Konjevic Polje and then embark upon liquidation and final liberation of the aforementioned areas." And again we see the term "liquidation" referred to there. Would your answer be as before, as to what that would refer to?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the word itself, "liquidation" refers to liquidating all living Muslims in the area. That's the meaning of the word "liquidation," to destroy, to kill, to exterminate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now continuing in that same paragraph, "At the same time, forces of the Bratunac Brigade, one battalion from the 1st forward defence line and the 3rd Infantry Battalion, shall conduct active operations and crush the enemy in the direction of the villages of Banjevici, Gornji Bacici, and Kravica. And special purpose units shall conduct offensive operations on the Sapotnik, Drenjak, Konjevici village axis. Forces of the Visegrad TG, tactical group, are to conduct full-scale active operations towards the general area of Gorazde." Now are you familiar with Banjevici and Gornji Bacici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What area are they in?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between Konjevic Polje and Kravica, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are either or both of them located near the road which you indicated yesterday on the map, the road from Zelinja into Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were you aware that there was combat activity in the Kravica area in February 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What date did you say, excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Continued combat operations. Let me -- in the Kravica area, in the period February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was there combat activity in the Konjevic Polje area in February 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Konjevic Polje, Cerska, and those parts, whereas the villages you have just mentioned, well, there were no people there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I would ask for an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document which consists of five pages in B/C/S and five pages in English with ERN 04336227 right through and inclusive of 04336231 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D882.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, we go back to D573, the War Presidency document, and we see an entry 11 March 1993, and the second paragraph, "General Morillon came to Srebrenica today." Were you aware of General Morillon's visit to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So would it be right that he arrived in Srebrenica in the midst of this catastrophic situation, as you've described it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then if we see the entry for 13 March 1993, it says, "At 0600 hours the Chetniks attacked and occupied Jagodnja. Fighting continued around Kragljivoda. The Biljeg and Poznanovici area was attacked. At about 0900 hours the Potocari area was attacked and at 1430 hours, two helicopters dropped chemical agents in the Biljeg area. During the day, seven civilians were killed and ten injured. At 1700 hours, an attack aircraft bombed the Biljeg and Pirici areas". Now, first, are you able to confirm the information in this entry and, if so, to what extent?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that this is correct, because I repeat, at that time, I was in the war hospital in Srebrenica, and every day wounded arrived from all the areas around Srebrenica. I always heard information from those whose wounds were not too serious or from people bringing the wounded in. So I can confirm that this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a document of the same date, a new exhibit, which is ERN 01332069. And in the interests of time I'll read into the record the following: It's the Bratunac Brigade command, 13 March 1993, regular combat report. And then I go to paragraph 2, "Our forces: During the day, our forces conducted forced reconnaissance and executed activities along the whole front line, especially on Pecista, Potocari, and Zagoni. Our frontline was moved approximately one kilometre forward to the Zuti Most towards Potocari." Now, pausing there, do you know Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zuti Most is between Potocari and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And can you help us with -- what sort of a situation was it on 13th of March 1993, with the Serbs so close to Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was critical. It was very bad. It was lucky that the UN turned up to prevent the Serbs from penetrating into the centre of town and massacring civilians. I have to mention that they did make use of the role of the UN and Philippe Morillon because, as he moved towards Srebrenica, they followed in his wake, tightening the circle more and more, moving their lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So when you say they did make use of the role of the UN and Philippe Morillon, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs, the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So are you saying they exploited the presence of Morillon in Srebrenica in order to tighten the circle around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In good measure.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Now, in terms of Potocari, this was the area you told us yesterday of Naser Oric, correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Naser Oric was born in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was he fighting in Potocari around this time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, to your knowledge, what was Naser Oric doing in this period we've been looking at with this War Presidency document from January to April 1993? If you know.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with his 20 or 30 men who were under his command, and he was where there was the most fierce fighting. In that period he was defending Potocari. That's where the situation was most critical in those days. To prevent the Serbs from penetrating into the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you know if Naser Oric was wounded in the course of this fighting?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was wounded in the leg, as far as I know. I think in mid-March 1993. And it was difficult for him to move around.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask for an exhibit number for this document and then we move to another exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document which consists of two pages, one in B/C/S, one in English, with ERN 01332069 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D883.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, in fact the next document is already an exhibit. There is D220 and D219. We have revised English translations because we noticed that the translation wasn't perfect. I don't know how Your Honours would propose to deal with that, if I were to tender the revised English translation, whether we can simply substitute it or whether it becomes a second translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, usually what we have done in the past rather than substituting is we add.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We just add it on. With the understanding that basically, unless there is an indication to the contrary, we will rely on the new document rather than the old.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is -- later on the problem is I don't replace one with the other because I don't -- the case doesn't end here. It ends whenever it ends. So up until the very end we may have a submission saying it's -- should look at one rather than the other or at both.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we leave them both there and then we see.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But there is going to be a declaration now in the record that this is according to you an updated translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I'm very much obliged. Thank you. So if the witness could be shown first D220?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, this document is headed Bosnia-Herzegovina, Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it's dated 2nd of August 2004. And I would draw your attention to the second paragraph. If you look at this document it says Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that Naser Oric was wounded once on the 12th of July 1992 in Zalazje and then again on 15 March 1993. "He was wounded by pieces of a tank grenade on defence in Pribicevac." Now, do you know where Pribicevac is?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is that location linked or not with the combat activities which we just looked at in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a single line, and there was a place there where the Serbs were already very, very close to the town, at the very entrance to the town, Pribicevac is to the east of Srebrenica. It's very close. And there was very fierce fighting going on there to prevent the Serbs from entering the town that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. You said in relation to this wound --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If Your Honours would give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. You said that Naser Oric was wounded in the leg and it was difficult for him to move around. Do you know if he was able to drive a car after he sustained that wound?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naser Oric was brought to hospital. I was in the hospital when he was brought in. They dressed his wound, gave him first aid, and took him away because there was no room in the hospital, only people who had been very seriously wounded were kept in the hospital. He couldn't move about, but in comparison with the other wounded his wound was not life-threatening and the situation in the hospital was so bad there weren't enough beds. There were wounded lying in the corridors, on the staircases; you could hardly move about the hospital for the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Did you actually ever see Naser Oric driving a car in Srebrenica? That's what I wanted to ask you about.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, very rarely did I see Naser Oric in Srebrenica at all, especially driving a car, no. No, the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I've finished with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, two things on this. Number 1 is the first of the two certificates, in other words the one which purports to be the translation of the 2nd August certificate -- in the English translation, confirming that Oric (Dzemal) Naset. That should be should be "Naser," not "Naset."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are correcting that. I suppose there is no objection on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a typing error. And secondly, all this will become, Madam Registrar, D20.1 -- 220.1, as it is, all documents, all right? Yes. Thank you. Yes. So we have dealt actually did that incorporate 219 as well before, Mr. Jones? Or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I haven't dealt with D219 and I propose to tender a revised translation of that exhibit as well which I think has been passed up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Because it's included in the documents that you have circulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's leave everything as D220.1, all right? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And then for the revised translation of D219 I suppose that would be D219.1 or you're putting the two together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm leaving everything as D220.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, returning to the War Presidency document, D573 I want to go now to the entry for the 16th of March 1993, so we are still progressing chronologically. And I'll just read into the record, "The aggressor occupied the Konjevic Polje area and torched villages in the region. The population withdrew towards Srebrenica, shelled by the enemy along the entire route to Srebrenica. Over 100 civilians killed and wounded. Fighting continued in the Kragljivoda area and an attempted infantry penetration into the Potocari sector." Now, are you familiar with the events described in this entry?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I want you to -- bearing that entry in mind -- now look -- if the witness could be shown D424, please. And this is a document of the command of the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade dated 16 March 1993, signed for the commander, Major Vinko Pandurevic. And I'm just going to read paragraphs 1 to 3. "After the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade units reached the Kravica sector, the Bratunac Light infantry Brigade units advanced along the Glogova, Planina mountain, Kravica axis. And the 2nd Birac Light Infantry Brigade along the Nova Kasaba, Pobrdje, Hajducko, Globlje axis. The enemy withdrew deeper towards Srebrenica and, unable to offer substantial resistance, fled, leaving heavy weapons behind. After yesterday's flight, our units -- fight, our units reached," and then various points are mentioned. "Two, the units of the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade carried out their task as set by the order of the corps command, strictly confidential number" - the number follows - "and reached the Lolici, Sandici, Doljani, Vis line to the west of the church in Kravica village, which is now being held by 2nd Infantry Battalion." "Three the new zone of responsibility along the line of Lolici, Sandici, Dolje Bezameni [phoen], Vis, to the west of the church in Kravica village, the 2nd PB has the task to fortify the line reached and persistently defend it." I want to ask you, where are those villages, Sandici and Lolici, in what area?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sandici and Lolici are located between Konjevic Polje and Kravica. Sandici is adjacent to Kravica and Lolici follows right behind it. Those are hamlets.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. We've seen this document is dated 16th March 1993, like the entry we saw in the War Presidency document. Does this information confirm or not the entry which we saw in the War Presidency document about combat activities in the Konjevic Polje area?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they do confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's clear this first. I thank you, Madam Vidovic, for bringing that to my attention. Are you receiving interpretation now, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And I heard the witness answering your question, so I just want to make sure that he was receiving interpretation at all times while the question was being put by Mr. Jones. In other words, that there was no interruption. If necessary, I will read out the question again to you and then you can answer it again, Mr. Sacirovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was receiving interpretation. I was able to hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. I think at this point we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, I've finished with D424.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In five minutes. Is it okay? Now it's better? All right. Mr. Jones, would you mind if we stopped here?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, certainly that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's break for 25 minutes starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you would like to make a statement, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Meanwhile we find out more information we want to convey that to you. Ms. Joanne Richardson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben. Madam Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That you, Your Honour. I will make it fast. Your Honour, we have investigated or looked into the matter of the disclosure of the documents we talked about this morning. Document ERN 01097642 was disclosed under receipt 226 A and that was done on the 23rd of September 2005. With respect to the other documents, it's my understanding that these were disclosed on the EDS Oric specific disclosure, which was a request from the Defence, and that was done on the 7th of October 2005. And that's on the EDS but specifically to the Oric -- Naser Oric case, to the Defence. And let me just say, Your Honour, notwithstanding our information -- I'm sorry, I just was informed under the Miroslav Deronjic file which was disclosed on the EDS to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Not the Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour but it was in response to the Oric Defence making a specific request. Let me just say as a practical matter if in the foot you are these documents -- that the Defence is unable to find these documents, we have absolutely no problem if they contact us and say, "We simply don't have them." We will be more than happy to provide a copy to them, give it to them, you know, whatever time at night in their locker. So, we can take a very practical approach to this in the future. And if they contact our case manager and she's not available, you know, they should contact as a matter of fact contact the attorney who will be taking the matter on. And we usually are in the office very late or that -- Jan Wubben who is also in the office fairly late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, you look into this matter I suppose Mr. Jones. But in the meantime let's not waste more time, please. Have the copies been made available in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, they have been provided to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, we will revisit this theme, that there is very much two sides to this story and certainly this is the information which the Prosecution has provided. Apart from the fact that, obviously, we will check it, we don't accept that -- that this is an accurate statement of affairs. We will look into it. It's particularly important because one is a prior statement allegedly of this witness, and we asked specifically from the Prosecution for any prior statements of our witnesses so that in particular we would be able to have them available for proofing. And if it turns out that this one alleged prior statement was not disclosed to us in time, so that we are started our examination-in-chief without having a document which we should have been provided in order to be able to proof him with it, then we would absolutely object to that document being used in cross-examination. The other thing is some of these documents we've now checked, appear to be Prosecution exhibits but we were provided the wrong ERN number. There is one ERN number which is crossed out and then another one and, if we had simply been told that one is P8, apparently one is P39, then we would have been able to find it. Instead, of course, we wasted a lot of time looking for documents under these ERN numbers. But in any event I'll reserve the bulk of my comments for another occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you both. When you -- if you -- if you wish to make further submissions on this, Mr. Jones, of course, you will be given all the opportunity. In the meantime let's move. Where is the usher? Yes, sorry. Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to add something to this matter because I am much more familiar with the documentation than my colleague. As for the Deronjic file, yes, we have received it and we received the document used yesterday, including some other documents. However, we know therefore very well what we received within the Deronjic file, where there was Mustafa Sacirovic's statement, as well as the document we used yesterday. But there was nothing else relating to Mr. Sacirovic. I told Ms. Richardson yesterday that they constantly fail to provide evidence to us. They did not even provide the audiotapes to us. Instead of supplying us with the material that the Defence needs for their preparation, they constantly come up with excuses to Your Honours. They have been constantly violating the 68 -- Rule 68 and 66, too, thus preventing us from preparing ourselves adequately for the Defence of our client, Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I will not be making any comments because I haven't seen these documents as of yet. I don't even know what the contents is and what they are about. So let's bring the witness in and we will address this matter later on, if and when necessary. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Sacirovic, we are going to remain a bit longer with this document, D573, the War Presidency document, and review a few more entries. I'm up to the 19th of March 1993 entry. If you can find that, I'll read that for the record. "At 0530 hours, two planes dropped chemical agents over the Osatnica MZ. Infantry attacks in the Kragljivoda, Osat, and Poznanovici sectors intensified with artillery support from Serbia and Jezero. Shelling of the Potocari and Srebrenica areas increased and there was an attempted infantry penetration in the Potocari sector. Eight civilians were killed and 18 wounded." Have you seen that entry?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you've already described the situation in Potocari in the days leading up to this. Was the situation in fact getting worse in this period?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was simply unbearable.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you can keep that document with you while we go to the next exhibit, which is a document of the same date, 19 March, 1993, the ERN is 04267595, and it's from the Drina corps command dated 19 March 1993, regular combat report to the RS Army Main Staff. And we see paragraph 2, "Combat readiness of our forces. During the day, forces of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade conducted activities in the following directions, Kravica, Bljecevo, Pale, Lemesic, Cizmici, Bijela Stijena, Zuti Most, Budak, Potocari, and Obadi, Zalazje, Likari." Now, are you familiar with those place names?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are they or some of them in the Potocari area?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bljeceva is adjacent to Potocari. Lemesic, Cizmici, are part of Bljeceva. Budak is also adjacent to Potocari and Bratunac. Obadi, Zalazje, Likari, are also adjacent to Potocari, to the east of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were you aware of activities of the Bratunac light Infantry Brigade or other Serb forces in those areas on that day?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can I please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Jones. This document which consists of two pages in B/C/S, two pages in English, being the translation, with ERN 04267595 to 596 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D884.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, the next document is D351, if the witness could be shown that, please. This is also 19 March 1993 from the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade Command to the command of the Drina Corps. And it says, "The Srebrenica operation is under way. On the Glogova, Pale, Potocari axis, tasks are being carried out according to plan with no particular problems." And then I move down to the reference to the Zuti Most area. My apologies. I'm going first to paragraph 2. "I successfully resolved the problems with UNPROFOR during the day." Does that -- that second paragraph, does that reflect in any way on what you told us earlier about how UNPROFOR, the presence of UNPROFOR in Srebrenica was exploited by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what's the problem, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no problem except that this is a single sentence and I don't believe, unless I'm mistaken, this witness can respond to Mr. Jones's question about problems with UNPROFOR. This is a very vague sentence here and I think any answer would be speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see. Let him answer first. I'm sure that if he's not in a position to answer or if he doesn't know what was the nature of any problems that might have existed with UNPROFOR at the time, he will not volunteer an answer. So let's proceed with your question, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps I might put it a different way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it would be wiser to put it, and more appropriate too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did the presence of UNPROFOR in Srebrenica in March 1993, did that in any way impede the Serb advance, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that you cannot agree on this. However, the very fact that UNPROFOR arrived in Srebrenica via Bratunac, where the Serb line moved by one kilometre from Zuti Most to Srebrenica, speaks for itself, indicates the fact that they used the passage of UNPROFOR and they were following in their footsteps and arrived almost to Potocari because Zuti Most and Potocari are very close by. So they must have been a very, very close to Potocari proper, the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was Potocari an important point in the defence of Srebrenica or not?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. There were factories in Potocari and Potocari was a very significant point, very close to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And if Potocari fell, what would have been the consequences for the defence of the enclave in March 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs would enter Srebrenica and probably massacre the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd simply ask for an exhibit number -- sorry, that's D351 so I don't need an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes it's already go one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Returning to the two last entries D573, the entry for 20th of March 1993. "At about 0530 hours chemical agents were dropped from a helicopter on Osmace. Attack on the Budak-Pale line, Potocari, Osmace and Skenderovici shelled. The aggressor captured some hill near Tokoljak, 684 civilians, women and children, evacuated to Tuzla." I would ask simply if you were able to confirm any of the events mentioned in that entry.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Which in particular, if you could elaborate?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA SACIROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, the dropping of chemical agents from helicopters, I was in the hospital close to the wounded who behaved strangely. You could see that they were experiencing hallucinations. They behaved strangely, which was probably a result of the chemical agents. As far as the evacuation of the civilians is concerned, the situation was chaotic. The UNPROFOR trucks that arrived in Srebrenica evacuated the civilian population. The town itself was overcrowded. There were close to 80.000 people within the limits of the town, and the situation was undescribable, close to a catastrophe. Had the Serbs entered the town, it would have been a catastrophe.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And we go to a document again of the Drina corps of the same date, 20th of March, 1993. This is a new exhibit, ERN 04267599. And this is, as I say, command of the Drina Corps, 20 March 1993, regular combat report to the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska. And I'm going to take to you paragraph 2, "level of combat readiness in our forces."
